#3813. Does GTA 6 have an 'easy mode'? Not officially, but there are two very important settings you can change to make the game less difficult

By now, you've probably heard that you cannot use cheats in GTA 6 until you complete the main story. Not only that, but enabling cheat codes also locks story progression and deactivates the ability to save. Basically, you can use cheats to have a quick crime spree and blow off some steam, then it's back to normalcy. Understandably, some gamers are a little put out with this change.

But, for anyone looking to have a slightly easier time with GTA 6 than the dev's intended experience, I come with good news: you can make the game a little bit easier by toggling two options in the game's Settings menu. If you open Settings, and then navigate to Gameplay, you'll find 'Accessible Combat' and 'Reduced Vehicle Damage' toggles. You can activate both to make GTA 6's more difficult elements a little bit easier to work through.

'Accessible Combat' decreases enemy health and makes them deal less damage to your character — the kind of rebalancing that you'd expect from a traditional difficulty slider. 'Reduced Vehicle Damage', as you'd expect, lowers the damage taken by your vehicle and allows your ride to endure more punishment. This applies to gunfire, environmental threats, and impact damage.

Toggle these settings comes with a warning from Rockstar, though. A prompt notes that enabling these modifiers will "significantly change the balance and experience of the gameplay". I've been playing around with these settings and whilst they are not a foolproof 'God Mode' by any means, you can absolutely see a difference in the game when they're enabled: Jason and Lucia take a lot more punishment from melee damage and gunshots, and I had to really try to get Jason's old banged up pickup into even the 'slightly smoking' bracket of disrepair. Your mileage may vary, but these settings, from what I can tell so far, certainly do make the game easier.

Given that cheats disable trophies and progression, these settings might be something to keep in mind if you're trying to find a smoother path through the main story of GTA 6. It's a credit to Rockstar's accessibility teams that these have been included at all - alongside the 23 other gameplay accessibility options, the 12 display options, the 70 UI options, the 24 camera options, and the 14 audio options.

"We create inclusive, intuitive, and immersive experiences for every player," noted Rockstar's associate UI director, Sam Grosset, in materials provided to Eurogamer ahead of the game's launch. "Accessibility is considered from the outset, and designing for diverse needs enables us to create better games for everyone. We wanted every player in GTA 6 to have options to play the game how they like. Whether it's selecting a larger font size, opting for a more minimal screen experience, or making a controls tweak to sprinting... the choices are open to all."

We also learned yesterday that Rockstar has made GTA 6 missions "harder to fail" by making them more open-ended, and giving players more ways to figure out how to do things in their own way.

If you need a hand with any of the myriad things GTA 6 asks you to do, you can read Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

#3812. Akira Kurabayashi, company director at Arika and developer on Street Fighter EX, Tetris 99, Fighting EX Layer and more, has sadly passed away due to heart failure

As announced in a statement by Arika president Akira Nishitani (and translated by Time Extension, thank you), Akira Kurabayashi, a director at the combined dev/publishing studio and a creator whose work spans three decades and several genres, sadly passed away as a result of heart failure late last week.

Kurabayashi initially worked as a programmer on smaller titles at Taito, including early 2.5D fighting game Fighters' Impact (later localised as VS. in America). He then moved to Arika in 1996 and continued his work in 2.5D fighters with the Street Fighter EX series, a subseries which took the originator of the fighting game genre into the third dimension for the first time. While that subseries didn't last long, its spiritual successor Fighting EX Layer made waves in 2018, bringing back original characters from SFEX and even including Fatal Fury's Terry Bogard.

Fighting EX Layer started out as an April Fools' joke back in 2017, but the reaction to the trailer from fans who missed the SFEX series convinced Arika to bring the series back, even without the Capcom IP. The final result is an interesting 2.5D fighter that combines conventional mechanics, such as magic series combos and supers, with the unique (for better and worse) Gougi system, where of in-match perks are chosen from a deck of cards at roundstart. I had a good time playing it for its systems (and Terry is very fun in it), but the Gougi system brought to mind Street Fighter x Tekken's infamous paid Gem debacle, which no one should be reminded of. Anyway. In addition to 2.5D fighters, Kurabayashi also contributed to Tetris: The Grandmaster, Tetris 99, PAC-MAN 99, and ARIKA's collaboration with SNK in the form of their 'SNK Revamp Project'.

Nishitani gave a few personal words towards Kurabayashi in the statement:

"We are deeply saddened to have lost a dear colleague who has created numerous works with us and supported Arika for many years. We express our heartfelt respect and gratitude for his immense achievements to date, and we will cherish and carry on the skills, experience, and attitude toward game development that he left behind. I would like to express my deepest gratitude for the kindness you showed us during their lifetime, and I respectfully pray for the repose of their soul."

UPDATE 5PM GMT: Actors Manni L. Perez and Dylan Rourke have announced their involvement in GTA 6, in portraying Lucia and Jason, respectively, in the game.

Dylan Rourke wrote on Instagram: "Years witnessing the hardest working and most skilled artisans game making has to offer. A photo accompanying the post shows the actors posing in front of a billboard advertising the game.

A post shared by Dylan Rourke (@dylan_rourke)

ORIGINAL STORY 3PM GMT: Rockstar has finally announced the full cast list for Grand Theft Auto 6, having left fans speculating right up to the game's release about which actors play the game's leads.

Lucia's actor Manni L. Perez was revealed through her nomination for The Game Awards, and it nearly took a photo taken by Lucia's stunt double Victoria Lee to reveal who played Jason.

"After keeping my mouth shut for YEEAARRSSS (and what feels like FOREVER!!!), I can finally share that I've been lucky enough to help bring Lucia to life as her main stunt double in Grand Theft Auto 6, along with a whole bunch of other characters stunts along the way!" A post shared by Victoria Lee (@victoria_lee_stunts)

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Stealing an ATM in GTA 6 requires a few different things: a winched vehicle to haul it out of the wall and drive off, plus the dye pack jammer that stops marked bills from exploding pink all over your lovely cash.

There are two ways to get a winched truck. The video above shows a location at the crop duster landing strip in Frogswater where you can steal one, but you can also mod any truck at a mod shop to add a winch.

If you don't have a truck to mod, there's a unique one you can steal from the Kolt & Associates June Warehouse robbery in Port Gellhorn, just south of Sarena's Bargain Store, which you could then register with Moses and mod at Wasteland Off-Road in the north of the town. You can also get a winched truck around the back of Yasmani's vape shop in Little Cuba—the fence who gives you the ATM tip offs.

You'll also need the dye pack jammer, which you get in the Chapter 3 main mission, Credit Check, for Raul. Once you have both of these, you're ready to rob an ATM. If you complete all three of Yasmani's jewelry thefts (also in Chapter 3), he'll call a little later and offer tips about full ATMs, giving you three for free that you have a 24 hour window to hit. Here's how to steal them

For Yasmani's tipped-off ATMs I got about 11k-ish per time, so not terrible, but likely not the best way to make money unless you get really efficient at it and invest in a proper getaway winch truck.

#3808. Vote now for 2026's RPS 100: Reader Edition

For the past six years, the team at RPS have got together to pick what we consider to be the best 100 games you can play on PC. There's very little science involved, and we try not to get too hung up on what games should make the cut. From year to year, our rankings and choices vary wildly as the formation and tastes of the team changes.

However, our definitive list isn't always met with a chorus of approval and cheers of 'Hear, hear!', "'Well done!', and 'Couldn't have said it better myself!', so we also have the RPS 100: Reader Edition. This is your chance to submit your ten favourite PC games of all time. Your votes will be tallied up with all the other submissions from our other readers and we will produce a list of the community's top 100.

We've just finished revealing what we currently consider to be the Best PC games of all time and now it's your turn.

Using this very Google Form you can submit up to ten votes for your favourite PC games of all time. I will then tally them up with all the other votes from RPS's readers and produce a list of the community's top 100.

Now, a note on scoring. The game you put in 10th place will be awarded one point, 9th place will be worth two, 8th place will be worth three, and so on until you reach your top pick, which will be worth ten points. Please write the full game name (and include the year of release if there are multiple titles in a series with the same name, such as Doom (1993) and Doom (2016)). If in doubt, check how the game is titled on Steam.

Last year, I implemented a change to create a greater variety of games on the list. I combined series scores, so if one reader voted for Civilization IV and another voted for Civilization VI, the scores of both were combined and the entry would be for the Civilization series. I also shared the breakdown of the votes for each title in the entry, so you could see which was most popular within the series.

I will be doing the same again this year, as we saw a lot more games that wouldn't have made the cut otherwise. However, I will try to do a better job of separating out games that are very different from one another even if they are in the same series. Warcraft 3 and World of Warcraft are both Warcraft games, but, admittedly, they aren't similar games. I would ask for some leeway on this, though, as not every example is clear cut. Should Alpha Centauri be counted among the Civilization games? Are Final Fantasy XIV and Final Fantasy Tactics - The Ivalice Chronicles truly worlds away from the other games in the Final Fantasy series?

This does also mean that one-shot games can struggle to compete against games which are part of longrunning series. After all, Crimson Skies isn't just competing against Microsoft Flight Simulator (2020), it is competing against votes for any and all Microsoft Flight Simulator games ever released. Unfortunately, this is a cost of the system, but I prefer the variety that comes from seeing more games represented instead of several separate entries for games within the same series.

We also invite you to tell us why you've chosen each game. This is entirely voluntary, you can simply enter the game titles if you would prefer. However, I'll choose a selection of what readers have said about winning games so we can better understand why the RPS community loves these games. Try not to write any more than 100 words. If you have more to say you can always drop it in the comments of the list when we publish it at the end of the year.

#3807. Black Friday GTA 6 deals LIVE: I'm finding the best ways to enhance your adventure in Leonida using 2026's end-of-year discounts

By now, you might be well into your adventure through Leonida, but Black Friday GTA 6 deals could take things a step further, or help you get the game for a lower price. Truth be told, there are loads of ways to enhance your enjoyment of the game. Whether you're coming back to gaming for the first time in ages or this is your full-time hobby and you want to see how a new controller, chair, headset, or screen might help you enjoy things more, I've got you.

See, I review all sorts of gaming hardware for my job, and part of that job is tracking the prices of all the latest gear throughout the year so I know when the best times to buy them are. No period of the year sees as many bits of gaming hardware with discounted price tags quite like Black Friday, and since GTA 6's launch has coincided with them this year, there are honestly so many things you could get for cheaper than usual that could enhance your playtime in GTA 6 for now, for the inevitable multiplayer launch, and beyond.

So I'm here to help. From now until the end of Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales, I'm going to be tracking down the best discounts for GTA 6 players. So far, I've found controllers, headsets, chairs, screens, and vouchers, just in case you haven't actually bought the game yet and you're looking for a cheaper route in. You'll find my favorite deals right below, but I'll be updating you live with my findings and shopping advice, so stick around and let's see what we find.

I've been reviewing PS5 and Xbox accessories and their deals for four years as GamesRadar+'s hardware editor. I'm also a huge GTA fan, so I'm excited to pull both of those things together for this live report to recommend you the gear that'll make your time with this much-anticipated game all the more special. I'm only going to recommend the stuff I've actually had hands-on time with, reviewed, and would happily use or recommend to a friend.

Favorite GTA games: GTA 4, GTA Online, GTA: San Andreas

If you've been waiting for a Black Friday deal to try and get GTA 6 a little more affordable, it's not currently on offer anywhere. The other option is to try to get GTA 6 digitally, and for that you might have better luck looking for discounted PSN vouchers.

UK: The game is actually discounted at Amazon in the UK, but there's a PSN wallet upgrade linked below too if you want to check that out.

For UK shoppers, things are a bit simpler. Not only is the game itself discounted at Amazon, but you can also get £10 off the cost of the digital version by purchasing this PSN voucher at ShopTo.

US: I'm not seeing an equivalent voucher deal for you folks, but check back soon to see what I find.

The DualSense Edge is, in my eyes, the best controller for GTA 6, and although its price is infamously stubborn, it's seeing a discount across the board in the UK and US.

The GameSir G7 Pro is the best controller for most players who don't want to break the bank on Xbox, but still want great functionality. There are options with larger feature sets I'll be seeking out, so stay tuned to the live updates further down the page, but when this is discounted, it's hard for most players to disagree with.

The Fractal Scape is a premium-feeling gaming headset at a mid-range price. It's one I use every day and although it won't be any help to Xbox players, it'll be an excellent choice for PS5 and PC players looking to grab a headset that punches above its weight in terms of audio quality.

For Xbox and PC players, the SteelSeries Arctis Nova 7 Gen 2 will strike a really nice balance between premium audio quality, a reasonable price tag, and a good mix of features and connectivity.

Read more: SteelSeries Arctis Nova 7 Gen 2 review

If you're noticing in your early weeks with GTA 6 that your old chair is getting a bit worse for wear, I'd recommend the Corsair TC500 Luxe. Especially for a more relaxed, comfy, and sturdy seat you'll want to spend lots of time in, this is one of my favorite console-leaning desk chairs.

Just in case anyone coming to this is worried - this blog is designed for all players, and to be safe, there will be nothing on this page that will present spoilers of GTA 6. If you're trying to steer clear of as much coverage and criticism as you can so you can make your own mind up, or generally just avoid spoilers as much as possible, don't worry!

I'm here to give you recommendations for enjoying the game, and I'm not about to ruin it for you.

There are loads of gaming chairs out there, so you might be wondering why I'd recommend the TC500 Luxe as the one most GTA players should think about.

I think the TC500 Luxe strikes such a fine balance of comfort and ergonomic support for your back. It's quite big and broad, and its cushioning is plush, its upholstery is soft, and it comes in a few classy colorways that'll help your setup look distinguished, but definitely a safe haven for your gaming time.

It's the sort of chair you'd be happy to sit in for hours and hours at a time without getting uncomfortable, and one you can relax into in so many different positions.

It essentially feels like a couch on wheels, and its price right now is $150 off, so you're genuinely getting a good bargain.

Corsair TC500 Luxe: $549 $409 at Amazon | £499 £349 at Amazon

Let's be honest, no one wants to stop playing, right? Whether it's healthy or not, finding a way to keep playing on the go could be massive for you if you're totally hooked on GTA 6. Gotta commute somewhere now that you're back to work? Gotta let someone else use the TV? Do you need a sneaky way to take GTA 6 with you when you're at a family gathering? I fully support you, even if I think taking breaks is also important.

A mobile controller is the key to all of this. Whether you're on Xbox or PlayStation, you can find ways to remote play and stream the game from your console at home to your mobile phone, and a good mobile gamepad will help you transition most naturally from one platform to the other.

My favorite mobile controller, the ELO Vagabond, is annoyingly not discounted anymore even though it was a week ago? Thanks for that one, ELO. But the GameSir G8 Galileo, my second favorite (which is actually cheaper), is discounted. It'll work for both PS5 and Xbox Remote Play, so enjoy!

GameSir G8 Galileo: $79.99 $63.99 at Amazon | £79.99 £59.99 at Amazon

While the UK is already enjoying discounted PS Store gift cards to use for a GTA 6 download, those deal hunting in the US would do well to keep in close comms with Newegg. The retailer is generally the most reliable place to find discount codes on these gift cards, regularly offering as much as $10 or $20 off higher amounts.

While these offers typically rear their heads towards the end of Black Friday, it's worth checking back regularly - they can move fast when they're live.

The SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Omni is down to $349.99 (its lowest price yet) at Amazon, but I'd recommend PS5 and Xbox Series X players turn their attention to the Nova Pro Wireless instead. You're still getting that quality SteelSeries audio, with the added perks of hot-swappable batteries and a clean, comfortable design - but without shelling out $350 on a headset with features you won't need. Let me explain.

The Omni has been designed as a true multi-platform device across both PC and consoles. That means it uses premium Hi-Res certification, only available on Windows. You won't be able to get the most out of these cups on PlayStation or Xbox.

Yes, it's the best gaming headset we've tested so far - but the Pro Wireless is easily the best value for GTA 6.

There is another complication for Xbox players. Right now, the Xbox version is out of stock at Amazon - but be sure to keep an eye out over the course of the sale.

SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Wireless (PlayStation) | $299.99 $229.99 at Amazon

I've been enjoying a whole new world of back buttons on PS5 since the Scuf Omega joined my setup this year, but GTA 6 has proven how much I miss those adaptive triggers every time I turn away from my OG DualSense. That's where the Edge has me in a chokehold.

Feeling that acceleration bump, shooting those rifles, even nailing the boards in Jason's house feels fantastic with these triggers under the hands. Playing without them feels like I'm missing half the experience.

That's why I'd typically recommend sticking with the DualSense itself for GTA 6 (thankfully they're still on sale). However, if you're looking to maximise inputs, those back nubbins on the DualSense Edge will give you the best of both worlds.

Sony's pro pad is down to $169.99 in this week's Black Friday GTA 6 deals, a rare $30 discount on the $199.99 MSRP.

DualSense Edge | $199.99 $169.99 at Amazon

I'll start off by checking to see if my own kit is up for grabs, and then move onto some of the top headsets I've had the pleasure of using in Vice City so far.

I was hoping we'd see a discount on the latest colorways of the GameSir G7 Pro, which are definitely not GTA 6 editions. Definitely not.

The Raiju V3 Pro is one for PS5 players to consider (I'll be back for an Xbox equivalent recommendation in a second).

It's a super responsive and clicky controller with mouse switch tech inside it to give it an instant actuation feel. It has four back buttons, two additional shoulder buttons, TMR thumbsticks, and they're symmetrical.

In other words, it's one of the most feature-rich PS5 pads out there, and it might even be more than most players will need for GTA 6. Either way, I didn't expect it to come this far down from its $210 price tag for Black Friday. Definitely one to think about.

Razer Raiju V3 Pro: $219.99 $189.99 at Amazon | £199.99 £149.99 at Amazon

I alluded to it before, but a set of speakers can be a really good asset to have in your gaming setup because it takes some of the direct pressure off your ears.

Did you know that it can cause damage to your hearing if you listen to music or play games through a headset for longer than 45 minutes at a time, if you listen at two-thirds of full volume? That's why a set of speakers can come in really, really handy - especially if you're playing GTA 6 in longer sessions.

There are multiple sets of speakers on sale right now that could really improve your setup. Here are some I'd recommend:

Officially licensed PS5 controllers don't come cheap, which is why deals on slightly older ones can come in really handy for big game releases like this. The Nacon Revolution 5 Pro has been a long-standing recommendation in the market from me, but it's recently been replaced by the Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited, an even better remodel of it.

That means a rare thing in the PS5 controller market - discounts on older gear!

The Nacon R5P is still a great controller, and one that will give you four back buttons and Hall sensor thumbsticks, as well as a box of goodies you can use to make it your own.

The only trade-off? It's a third-party licensed controller, which means it won't have access to the haptics and adaptive trigger resistance of the DualSense or DualSense Edge. That's the eternal toss-up, so I'll let you decide.

Nacon Revolution 5 Pro: $149.99 at Amazon

In a word, yes. In my opinion, OLED TVs are always going to be worth it, and the problems surrounding burn-in are just not what they used to be.

The problem is that they're more expensive, and that sucks. I'm a massive believer in OLED tech; I think it makes a massive difference to the visuals in games and movies, but there's no avoiding the extra expense that comes with them.

Here's the thing: OLEDs aren't the only option, and the main reason I got the LG OLED C4 was for its stunning panel, but also its 144Hz refresh rate for PC gaming.

In my opinion, these OLED TVs with faster refresh rates are amazing, but you can get excellent visuals with more affordable panels - you don't need an OLED to make GTA 6 look great. If GTA 6 is only going to run at 30fps for the foreseeable future, it's probably not worth investing in one for that reason only.

On the other hand, if you want the best of the best TVs going so you can bring out the stunning visuals Rockstar has crafted, OLED is unbeatable.

The PowerA Fusion Pro Wireless might have its clever ghost RGB to lure you in, but I think this is one of the most underrated Xbox controllers of the generation. It's got four back buttons, wireless play, a charging stand, and twisty thumbsticks you can use to adjust their height.

All that, and it's under $100 right now - huge for getting as much controller as you can for your money at the moment. Remember, this thing launched at $149.99.

PowerA Fusion Pro Wireless: $149.99 $89.99 at Amazon | £149.99 £69.99 at Amazon

So, first up is the chair I'd argue is the best overall for anyone sitting at a desk or a gaming setup for long hours of the day. It's called the LiberNovo Omni, which launched on Kickstarter last year and quickly took over the market. It's since expanded into a few different models: there's the normal Omni, which is strangely MIA for this Black Friday; there's the Pro model, which features electronics within that enhance the experience, and there's the SE model, which has the same revolutionary backrest design but a mechanical backrest adjustment system as opposed to a motorized one.

The reason this chair rules is that it features what this brand calls an omni-flex backrest. Its backrest has these spines that mimic the anatomy of your back, and there are loads of flex points that mean it rotates, pivots, and moves around with you as you're resting in it, all the while supporting your posture in a healthy way.

So, the Pro model is on sale as well, but it's still close to a grand, which I think is a bit pricey for anyone. I'll link to it below, but the one I'd recommend to most GTA 6 players this Black Friday looking for a little more back support and a comfier place to sit is the SE model.

And yes, I'll come back with some much more affordable choices in a second too.

Are you playing on the couch, or at a desk?

I'd guess that since Rockstar is neglecting the comparatively massive PC market, the majority of you will be playing GTA 6 on a big, comfy couch, but a lot of folks have dual setups around a desk these days, and some people don't have the room for a couch in their bedroom where they actually spend time gaming.

So with that in mind, I'm going to be recommending some gaming chairs here as well. GTA 6 is an experience you'll probably put over 100 hours into if you want to see everything and complete the main story without rushing, and that's a long old time to be sitting on a desk chair that you've probably been meaning to replace for a few years now anyway.

I also review gaming chairs, so I can give you a few pointers. What I will say is that gaming chairs rarely get more affordable throughout the year than they do during Black Friday, and since they're pretty stupidly expensive, it's a pretty good idea to buy one while they're actually a little more in budget. So coming up next, I'll show you one of my favorite chairs that's currently on offer, as well as a more budget-friendly alternative.

A week or two ago, I actually put together a list of controllers I've reviewed that I think would work wonders in GTA 6. I separated things out for Xbox and PC players, I gave a rundown of options to cover different budgets, and I think the majority of the ones I recommended over there are actually on sale, so I'll run through them one by one as we go, but if you know you're looking for a controller for GTA 6, it might be worth taking a quick look at the link below.

The first deal I'd like to bring to your attention is the Nacon Revolution X Unlimited.

This is one for the Xbox players, so PS5 readers, check back in a moment because I swear I love you all equally.

The Nacon RXU is my favorite controller for Xbox overall. It's one of the premium, elite gamepads for that console and features maybe the best microswitch buttons I've ever pressed. Alongside its prowess as a great gamepad doing the basics well, it has four back buttons, two additional bumpers, and a screen to help you customize it on a software level.

On the hardware level, it comes with a wireless dongle, a carry case, charging stand, tiny weights you can put in its grips, and swappable thumbstick tops to throw on its Hall sensor innards.

Unlike PS5 players, Xbox Series X and S gamers have even more of a reason to opt for a third-party licensed controller because they aren't bound to the same rigid licensing limitations that Sony ones are. They have rumble and haptic motors within them that are able to fire while you're playing on the console. PS5 controllers don't get that, so this is one you can rub in PS5 players' faces.

If you want to. I'm not fueling the console war. As I said, I love you both equally.

Nacon Revolution X Unlimited: $199.99 $149.99 at Amazon

When will Black Friday GTA 6 deals start to disappear?

Black Friday is tomorrow at the time of writing, that means it's Thanksgiving right now (so Happy Thanksgiving to all who celebrate) and deals are already underway. Discounts started to show a week or two ago, but will last probably through the weekend and eventually turn into Cyber Monday ones thereafter.

I'd be watching like a hawk today and tomorrow if there's something you're specifically looking for. Prices tend to hold throughout the weekend, but with so much renewed interest in gaming at the moment thanks to GTA, stock might not last as long as we want it to. Hope that helps!
